evidence.text:
Crystal Structures
Crystal structures can be described using a fundamental unit, such as a prim-
itive cell, conventional unit cell, Bravais lattice, or asymmetric unit, together with its associated
atoms.
The unit is defined by a 3 × 3 lattice matrix that specifies its geometry in real space.
Formally, a crystal structure is represented as M = (A, P, L), where A denotes atomic types,
P = [p1, . . . , pN] ∈R3×N contains the fractional or Cartesian coordinates of the N atoms, and
L = [ℓ1, ℓ2, ℓ3] ∈R3×3 defines the periodic lattice in real space.

Graph embedding
A crystal structure is represented as a graph G = (V, E), where vertices V =
{v1, v2, . . . , vN} correspond to atoms one-hot encoded attributes (Xie & Grossman, 2018) and
edges E ⊆V × V encode atomic interactions within a cutoff radius.

stage_name_raw: deriving analytical constraints on Fourier coefficients
stage_goal: To analytically derive the explicit linear constraints imposed by crystallographic symmetries on the Fourier coefficients of functions defined over Euclidean space.

evidence.text: Our goal is to find a universal representation for the constraints imposed by invariance to a crystallographic group G. We achieve this by analyzing the effect of group operations on the Fourier transform of a G-invariant function f : Rn →R.

Proposition 3.1. Let f : Rn →R be a G-invariant function and let F(ω) be its Fourier transform. All symmetry operations ϕ ∈G have the form ϕ(x) = Ax + t, where A is an orthogonal matrix and t is a translation vector. For any ϕ ∈G, the Fourier coefficients must satisfy the following relation for all ω ∈L∗: F(ω) = ei2πω⊤A⊤tF(Aω).

stage_name_raw: constructing symmetry-adapted Fourier basis via dual graph representation
stage_goal: To operationalize the analytical constraints by constructing a dual graph representation and using it to algorithmically generate the symmetry-adapted Fourier basis.

evidence.text: The algebraic relationships and phase constraints from Proposition 3.1 can be captured as a directed graph on the reciprocal lattice. In this graph, nodes represent frequencies ω ∈L∗, and each symmetry operation ϕ(x) = Ax + t induces a set of directed edges.
evidence.section: DUAL GRAPHS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC FOURIER SERIES
